habitat: Pairs when breeding, otherwise small flocks over open country, montane grassland, culverts, rocky koppies and around people.
summary: A common summer resident. Chestnut cap, pale chestnut rump, metallic-blue upper parts, and lightly streaked whitish underparts that look almost white in flight. The flight call is a soft chissik. The song is a pleasant trill and warble. It glides a lot and perches on trees and wires. Months were left unset. The Kemp code VB was left unchanged.

similar.note: Lesser Striped Swallow is much more heavily streaked below, and the orange cap covers the ear coverts.

population.notes: Kemp et al. 2001 order-of-magnitude threshold 2^7=128 mature individuals (visiting breeder); paper interval half–double → 64–256.

sources.title: Kemp A.C., Herholdt J.J., Whyte I. & Harrison J. (2001). Birds of the two largest national parks in South Africa: a method to generate estimates of population size for all species and assess their conservation ecology. S. Afr. J. Sci. 97: 393–403.

upperparts.pattern: Metallic blue, with a pale chestnut rump.

underparts.pattern: Lightly streaked. Almost white in flight.

viewNotes.note: Chestnut cap, pale chestnut rump and lightly streaked whitish underparts.
Metallic-blue upper parts and a pale chestnut rump.
It flies with much gliding. The underparts look almost white.

calls.description: A soft chissik in flight. The song is a pleasant trilling and warbling, not given a separate file. Grade A call from the Drakensberg above Monk’s Cowl. The filename names Greater Striped Swallow. The filename also contains 28_B; the catalogue grade is A.
